_comment: SxS Overall Paper Quality — Run 2 of 2 (positional-bias mitigation). ORDER SWAPPED: paper_1 = original human-authored draft; paper_2 = paper-orc generated.
paper_1_holistic_analysis: Paper 1 (the human-authored draft) opens with a five-paragraph Introduction that names six recent LLM-personality critiques (Suhr 2025; Tjuatja 2023; Acerbi 2024; Salecha 2024; Pelet 2025; Huang 2024) and stakes the contribution in a single declarative sentence ('We do.'). The Related Work is organised into three subsections, each closing with an 'Our contribution' \paragraph that explicitly differentiates the present audit from the cited literature. The Methodology presents Cronbach's alpha as a numbered display equation and gives a more elaborate prose description of the EFA / parallel-analysis pipeline. Subsection titles in the Experiments and Results are deliberately narrative ('Caught in the Act', 'The Cascade') — engaging but slightly less neutral for an academic venue. The figure set is rich (research-question concept, methodology pipeline, scree+loadings, response styles, item plasticity, model dashboard) and includes a dedicated methodology overview diagram. Citation density across Intro and Related Work is 26 unique works, roughly 50% of the assumed ACL baseline; foundational methodological anchors (Kaiser, Horn, Tucker, Couch & Keniston, Crowne & Marlowe, Vandenberg & Lance, Meredith) are absent from those sections and instead appear sparingly later in Methodology.
paper_2_holistic_analysis: Paper 2 (the paper-orc output) opens with a causal-chain teaser figure and an Introduction that explicitly frames the silicon-sample programme as the downstream stakeholder of the validity audit. The Related Work spans three structured subsections, each closing with a 'bridge-to-our-method' synthesis sentence and citing 57 unique works including foundational anchors (Cronbach 1951; Couch & Keniston 1960; Crowne & Marlowe 1960; Kaiser 1958, 1960; Horn 1965; Tucker 1951; Meredith 1993; Vandenberg & Lance 2000). The 7-item itemised contribution list at the end of the Introduction provides a sharper preview than a prose paragraph. Methodology is consolidated into four \paragraph-level blocks rather than separate subsections, which compresses the formal presentation but maintains coverage of every check. Experiments use neutral diagnostic subsection titles ('Internal consistency: alpha tracks reverse density at rho = -1.0', 'Factor structure: 5 expected, 3 observed, universally'). Figures use a unified academic palette and consistent caption format; the appendix carries the long EFA loadings table, the per-model PSD, the persona-fidelity confusion matrix, and the within-sample consistency analysis. Total length fits the 8 content-page ACL EMNLP review limit; refs.bib is verified end-to-end (no orphan citations); anti-leakage post-check is clean.
comparison_justification: On Scientific Depth and Soundness, Paper 1's Cronbach display equation and more detailed parallel-analysis description give it a measurable edge over Paper 2's compressed Methodology; both papers, however, report the same numerical evidence and reach the same conclusions. On Technical Execution, both papers describe the same six-check + persona-stress pipeline and report identical numbers; tie. On Organization and Logical Flow, Paper 2's causal-chain teaser, parallel Related-Work subsection structure (overview → SOTA → limitation → bridge), and 7-bullet contribution list provide more explicit scaffolding for the reader than Paper 1's prose-only narrative. On Clarity and Precision, Paper 2 is tighter; Paper 1's evocative subsection titles ('Caught in the Act', 'The Cascade') are memorable but slightly less neutral for a top-tier ACL venue. On Presentation of Evidence, both papers carry ~20 figures and integrate them effectively; Paper 2 has a small edge in unified visual style and consistent figure-reference patterns. On Professional Academic Style, Paper 2's exclusive use of \citep / \citet is more ACL-canonical than Paper 1's mixed \cite usage. The decisive criterion is again the literature review: Paper 2 cites 57 unique works including the foundational psychometric anchors (Cronbach 1951, Kaiser 1960, Horn 1965, Tucker 1951, Couch & Keniston 1960, Crowne & Marlowe 1960, Vandenberg & Lance 2000, Meredith 1993) that Paper 1 omits from Intro / Related Work. For a paper whose central thesis is that the LLM-personality literature has skipped the standard human-subjects validation toolkit, citing that toolkit explicitly is a load-bearing element. Paper 2 wins after accounting for these differences.
